example_sentences.de: Wie geht es der Familie?
example_sentences.en: How is the family doing?

example_sentences.de: Und wie geht es deiner Familie in der Türkei?
example_sentences.en: And how is your family in Turkey doing?

cloze.de: Grüß deine Frau von mir, und wie ___ es der Familie?
cloze.en: Say hi to your wife from me, and how is the family doing?

words.notes: Dative after 'Wie geht es …': der Familie, deiner Mutter, den Kindern. Neutral register, works with du and Sie. Typical reply: 'Danke, allen geht es gut.'
words.germany_context: Colleagues do ask this in passing, but a short 'Danke, alles gut' is the expected answer — long family details are unusual at work.

example_sentences.de: Warst du schon mal in München?
example_sentences.en: Have you ever been to Munich?

example_sentences.de: Waren Sie schon mal in der Türkei?
example_sentences.en: (formal) Have you ever been to Turkey?

cloze.de: Warst du eigentlich ___ mal auf dem Oktoberfest?
cloze.en: Have you actually ever been to Oktoberfest?

words.notes: 'schon mal' means 'ever, at least once'. Informal du-form; formal is 'Waren Sie schon mal …?'. Typical reply: 'Ja, einmal.' or 'Nein, noch nie.'

translations: do you have brothers or sisters?

example_sentences.de: Hast du Geschwister?
example_sentences.en: Do you have siblings?

example_sentences.de: Haben Sie Geschwister?
example_sentences.en: (formal) Do you have siblings?

cloze.de: Bist du Einzelkind oder hast du ___?
cloze.en: Are you an only child or do you have siblings?

words.notes: 'Geschwister' is plural only — never 'ein Geschwister'. Informal; formal is 'Haben Sie Geschwister?'. Typical reply: 'Ja, zwei Brüder.' or 'Nein, ich bin Einzelkind.'

example_sentences.de: Wo kommst du ursprünglich her?
example_sentences.en: Where are you originally from?

example_sentences.de: Wo kommen Sie ursprünglich her?
example_sentences.en: (formal) Where are you originally from?

cloze.de: Und wo kommst du ___ her?
cloze.en: And where are you originally from?

words.notes: Spoken German splits 'woher' into 'Wo … her?'. Informal; formal is 'Wo kommen Sie ursprünglich her?'. Typical reply: 'Ursprünglich aus Izmir.'
words.germany_context: You will be asked this often once people hear an accent. It is usually friendly curiosity, but among younger Germans the wording is seen as loaded — 'Wo bist du aufgewachsen?' is the safer version to use yourself.

words.translation: what do you miss the most?
translations: what do you miss the most?

example_sentences.de: Was vermisst du am meisten an der Türkei?
example_sentences.en: What do you miss the most about Turkey?

example_sentences.de: Am meisten vermisse ich das Essen meiner Mutter.
example_sentences.en: What I miss the most is my mother's cooking.

cloze.de: Was ___ du am meisten aus deiner Heimat?
cloze.en: What do you miss the most from your home country?

words.notes: 'vermissen' takes a plain accusative object: 'Ich vermisse meine Familie.' Informal; formal is 'Was vermissen Sie am meisten?'. Replies usually start with 'Am meisten vermisse ich …'.

example_sentences.de: Ist das dein Ernst? Das kann doch nicht sein!
example_sentences.en: Are you serious? That just can't be!

example_sentences.de: Ist das Ihr Ernst?
example_sentences.en: (formal) Are you serious?

cloze.de: Zweihundert Euro für die Reparatur? Ist das dein ___?
cloze.en: Two hundred euros for the repair? Are you serious?

words.notes: Informal and a bit confrontational — signals disbelief. Formal: 'Ist das Ihr Ernst?'. Short spoken version: 'Im Ernst?'.

example_sentences.de: Das ist ja verrückt! Wie ist das passiert?
example_sentences.en: That's crazy! How did that happen?

example_sentences.de: Zehn Jahre Wartezeit? Das ist ja verrückt!
example_sentences.en: Ten years of waiting? That's crazy!

cloze.de: Du hast ihn zufällig in Istanbul getroffen? Das ist ___ verrückt!
cloze.en: You met him by chance in Istanbul? That's crazy!

words.notes: The 'ja' here is not 'yes' — it is a particle that adds astonishment. Informal reaction, but fine with Sie too. Typical follow-up: 'Erzähl mal!'.

words.word: Da bin ich ganz bei dir.
words.lemma: Da bin ich ganz bei dir
words.translation: I'm completely with you on that
translations: I'm completely with you on that

example_sentences.de: Da bin ich ganz bei dir, das sehe ich auch so.
example_sentences.en: I'm completely with you on that, I see it the same way.

example_sentences.de: Da bin ich ganz bei Ihnen.
example_sentences.en: (formal) I'm completely with you on that.

cloze.de: Was die Mieten angeht, da bin ich ___ bei dir.
cloze.en: As far as rents are concerned, I'm completely with you.

words.notes: Strong agreement without repeating the argument. Informal with 'dir', formal with 'Ihnen' — both are common in meetings.

example_sentences.de: Du bist müde? Das kann ich gut verstehen.
example_sentences.en: You're tired? I can totally understand that.

example_sentences.de: Ich kann gut verstehen, dass du Heimweh hast.
example_sentences.en: I can well understand that you're homesick.

cloze.de: Dass du am Anfang Heimweh hattest, das kann ich gut ___.
cloze.en: That you were homesick at the beginning, I can totally understand.

words.notes: Standard empathy move, stronger than a bare 'Ich verstehe.'. Neutral register — fine at work and with friends.

words.translation: what do you mean by that?
translations: what do you mean by that?

example_sentences.de: Wie meinst du das genau?
example_sentences.en: What exactly do you mean by that?

example_sentences.de: Wie meinen Sie das?
example_sentences.en: (formal) What do you mean by that?

cloze.de: Entschuldigung, wie ___ du das?
cloze.en: Sorry, what do you mean by that?

words.notes: Asks about someone's intention or opinion. For an unknown word use 'Was bedeutet das?' instead. Informal; formal is 'Wie meinen Sie das?'.

words.translation: can you explain that in more detail?
translations: can you explain that in more detail?

example_sentences.de: Kannst du das bitte genauer erklären?
example_sentences.en: Can you please explain that in more detail?

example_sentences.de: Können Sie das genauer erklären?
example_sentences.en: (formal) Could you explain that in more detail?

cloze.de: Ich habe das nicht ganz verstanden — kannst du das ___ erklären?
cloze.en: I didn't quite understand that — can you explain it in more detail?

words.notes: Add 'bitte' to soften it. Informal; formal is 'Können Sie das genauer erklären?'. Very useful in meetings when you missed a detail.

words.translation: what do you think of that?
translations: what do you think of that?
how do you feel about that?

example_sentences.de: Was hältst du davon, morgen ins Kino zu gehen?
example_sentences.en: What do you think about going to the cinema tomorrow?

example_sentences.de: Was halten Sie von dem Vorschlag?
example_sentences.en: (formal) What do you think of the proposal?

cloze.de: Wir könnten am Samstag grillen — was ___ du davon?
cloze.en: We could have a barbecue on Saturday — what do you think of that?

words.notes: 'halten von' means 'to think of'. Irregular: du hältst, er hält. Informal; formal is 'Was halten Sie davon?'. Typical reply: 'Gute Idee!' or 'Eher nicht.'

words.translation: I see it exactly the same way
translations: I see it exactly the same way

example_sentences.de: Ich sehe das genauso wie du.
example_sentences.en: I see it exactly the same way you do.

example_sentences.de: Bei diesem Punkt sehe ich das genauso.
example_sentences.en: On this point I see it exactly the same way.

cloze.de: Du hast völlig recht, ich sehe das ___.
cloze.en: You're absolutely right, I see it exactly the same way.

words.notes: Direct opposite of 'Das sehe ich anders.'. Neutral register — safe at work and with friends alike.
synonyms: Da bin ich ganz bei dir

words.translation: for me it's the other way around
translations: for me it's the other way around

example_sentences.de: Du arbeitest morgens am besten? Bei mir ist es umgekehrt.
example_sentences.en: You work best in the mornings? For me it's the other way around.

example_sentences.de: Bei mir ist es genau umgekehrt.
example_sentences.en: For me it's exactly the other way around.

cloze.de: Du magst Winter lieber als Sommer? Bei mir ist es ___.
cloze.en: You like winter better than summer? For me it's the other way around.

words.notes: A friendly way to disagree by contrast instead of contradiction. Neutral register; works with du and Sie.

words.word: Das ist mir auch schon passiert.
words.lemma: Das ist mir auch schon passiert
words.translation: that has happened to me too
translations: that has happened to me too

example_sentences.de: Keine Sorge, das ist mir auch schon passiert.
example_sentences.en: Don't worry, that has happened to me too.

example_sentences.de: So etwas ist mir auch schon passiert.
example_sentences.en: Something like that has happened to me too.

cloze.de: Du hast den Zug verpasst? Das ist mir auch schon ___.
cloze.en: You missed the train? That has happened to me too.

words.notes: 'passieren' takes the dative person (mir, dir, ihm) and builds the Perfekt with 'sein', not 'haben'. Neutral register; a classic way to make someone feel better.

example_sentences.de: Montagmorgen im Büro? Das kenne ich.
example_sentences.en: Monday morning at the office? I know that feeling.

example_sentences.de: Das kenne ich nur zu gut.
example_sentences.en: I know that feeling all too well.

cloze.de: Wartezeiten beim Amt? Das ___ ich leider auch.
cloze.en: Waiting times at the public office? Unfortunately I know that feeling too.

words.notes: Sympathy marker: means 'I have been through the same', not 'I am acquainted with it'. Informal but very common.
synonyms: Das ist mir auch schon passiert

example_sentences.de: Du warst im Urlaub? Erzähl mal!
example_sentences.en: You were on holiday? Do tell!

example_sentences.de: Erzählen Sie mal, wie war die Reise?
example_sentences.en: (formal) Do tell, how was the trip?

cloze.de: Wie war das Vorstellungsgespräch? ___ mal!
cloze.en: How was the job interview? Do tell!

words.notes: Imperative of 'erzählen' plus the particle 'mal', which turns an order into a friendly invitation. Informal; formal is 'Erzählen Sie mal.'.

example_sentences.de: Und dann? Was hat er gesagt?
example_sentences.en: And then? What did he say?

example_sentences.de: Und dann bin ich einfach nach Hause gegangen.
example_sentences.en: And then I just went home.

cloze.de: Du hast ihn angerufen — und ___? Was ist passiert?
cloze.en: You called him — and then? What happened?

words.notes: The cheapest way to keep someone's story going. Neutral register, works with du and Sie. As a statement opener the verb follows immediately: 'Und dann bin ich …'.

example_sentences.de: Du bist nach Deutschland gezogen — wie kam das?
example_sentences.en: You moved to Germany — how did that come about?

example_sentences.de: Und wie kam das mit dem neuen Job?
example_sentences.en: And how did that come about with the new job?

cloze.de: Ihr habt euch in Berlin kennengelernt? Wie ___ das?
cloze.en: You met each other in Berlin? How did that come about?

words.notes: 'kam' is the Präteritum of 'kommen'. Asks for the backstory, not for the method. Neutral register.

example_sentences.de: Zum Glück hat es nicht geregnet.
example_sentences.en: Luckily it didn't rain.

example_sentences.de: Der Zug hatte Verspätung, aber zum Glück nur zehn Minuten.
example_sentences.en: The train was delayed, but luckily only ten minutes.

cloze.de: ___ Glück war die Apotheke noch offen.
cloze.en: Luckily the pharmacy was still open.

words.notes: Word order: when 'Zum Glück' starts the sentence, the verb comes straight after it. Neutral register. Opposite: 'leider'.

example_sentences.de: Oje, das tut mir leid!
example_sentences.en: Oh dear, I'm sorry about that!

example_sentences.de: Oje, hast du dich verletzt?
example_sentences.en: Oh dear, did you hurt yourself?

cloze.de: ___, das klingt ja gar nicht gut.
cloze.en: Oh dear, that doesn't sound good at all.

words.notes: Sympathetic reaction to bad news. Informal but harmless in any company. Stronger version: 'Oh nein!'.

example_sentences.de: Naja, so schlimm war es auch nicht.
example_sentences.en: Well, it wasn't that bad either.

example_sentences.de: Wie war der Film? — Naja, es geht.
example_sentences.en: How was the film? — Well, it was okay.

cloze.de: ___, ganz zufrieden bin ich mit der Wohnung nicht.
cloze.en: Well, I'm not entirely happy with the apartment.

words.notes: Hedging filler signalling mild reservation or a 'so-so' answer. Very informal and extremely frequent in speech. Also written 'Na ja'.

example_sentences.de: Die Bürokratie ist langsam, das ist halt so.
example_sentences.en: The bureaucracy is slow, that's just how it is.

example_sentences.de: Das ist halt so in einer großen Stadt.
example_sentences.en: That's just how it is in a big city.

cloze.de: Sonntags sind alle Läden zu — das ist ___ so.
cloze.en: All the shops are closed on Sundays — that's just how it is.

words.notes: 'halt' is a resigned filler particle (southern and standard spoken German); 'eben' is the northern equivalent. Informal.
words.germany_context: You will hear this a lot about rules nobody questions any more — Sunday closures, Ruhezeit, paperwork. It politely means 'there is no point arguing'.

example_sentences.de: Apropos Wochenende, hast du schon Pläne?
example_sentences.en: Speaking of the weekend, do you have plans yet?

example_sentences.de: Apropos Arbeit — wie läuft dein neues Projekt?
example_sentences.en: Speaking of work — how is your new project going?

cloze.de: ___ Urlaub: Wann fährst du eigentlich?
cloze.en: Speaking of holidays: when are you actually going?

words.notes: Topic switch that picks up a word the other person just said. Neutral register, borrowed from French, stress on the last syllable.

example_sentences.de: Jedenfalls habe ich die Wohnung dann doch bekommen.
example_sentences.en: Anyway, in the end I did get the apartment.

example_sentences.de: Es war anstrengend, aber jedenfalls hat alles geklappt.
example_sentences.en: It was exhausting, but in any case everything worked out.

cloze.de: ___ war der Abend am Ende richtig schön.
cloze.en: Anyway, the evening turned out really nice in the end.

words.notes: Wraps up a digression and returns to the main point. Neutral register. At the start of a sentence the verb comes right after it.

example_sentences.de: Wie auch immer, wir sehen uns morgen.
example_sentences.en: Anyway, we'll see each other tomorrow.

example_sentences.de: Wie auch immer man das nennt, es funktioniert.
example_sentences.en: Whatever you call it, it works.

cloze.de: ___ auch immer — lass uns über etwas anderes reden.
cloze.en: Anyway — let's talk about something else.

words.notes: Closes a topic and can sound slightly dismissive. Informal to neutral; the formal written version is 'Wie dem auch sei'.
